newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican autopsy adds new twist to Salinas case.
newsitem.headline: Mexican autopsy adds new twist to Salinas case.

text.p: The mystery in Mexico surrounding a skeleton uncovered near the country home of Raul Salinas de Gortari grew deeper on Friday when autopsy results showed that a key Salinas associate was not the deceased.
"It's obvious that we cannot say that (the bones belong to) this person," the coroner who performed the autopsy told TV Azteca.
Raul Salinas is brother of disgraced former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, who is now in self-imposed exile in Ireland.
Raul Salinas is in jail on charges he ordered the 1994 assassination of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, the ruling party's secretary-general and his own former brother-in-law.
The arrest of Salinas was unprecedented in the Mexican political system, whose unwritten laws forbade any action against a former president or his family.

When the bones were uncovered on Salinas's ranch earlier this month, speculation swirled that they belonged to former Congressman Manuel Munoz Rocha, an associate of Salinas who disappeared shortly after the murder of Ruiz Massieu.
The triggerman in the Ruiz Massiueu murder identified Munoz Rocha as the man who paid him for the deed.
Morever, witnesses in the case claim that Raul Salinas killed Munoz Rocha by smacking him in the head with a baseball bat, local newspapers reported.
The coroner said the skeleton did not match Munoz Rocha's height.
